…to present to His Majesty.

Third Question
Jin Xian

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor (jiaoyu): In a policy essay on historical figures, only someone with an established foundation of learning and discernment can assess their relative merits. The candidates writing in the examination hall variously agree and disagree, without any settled judgment. This essay displays discrimination and decisiveness. Is its author not someone who befriends the worthy across the ages and, when duty calls, yields to no one?

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor (xuezheng): Comparing people whose qualities seem difficult to distinguish and discussing events that appear similar is precisely how we seek to observe candidates’ learning in the investigation of principle. This answer is accurate and detailed in its treatment of events, comprehensive yet concise in its language. In assessing the hidden subtleties of the motives and conduct of figures across hundreds and thousands of years, and their relative standing and importance, it errs not by the smallest fraction. His future achievements should offer much to admire.

Comment by Examiner Wen, Left Exhorter of Virtue: Plain and accessible, yet the language remains orderly throughout. Knowing what you have within you, how could your abilities be confined to discussing people who lived a thousand years ago?

Comment by Examiner Li, Expositor-in-Waiting: The deeds of the ancients are scattered throughout the histories. He brings them forward and discusses them, handling each one fittingly. He resembles a seasoned official of the Han court seated in judgment on doubtful cases: once he utters a brief pronouncement, neither right nor wrong can escape detection. Admirable! Admirable!

I have long held that, when discussing events already past, one should examine the difficulties and opportunities presented by their times and circumstances; when discussing people of the past, one should investigate whether their intentions were perverse or upright. Affairs in the world have no constant pattern. If one does not examine the difficulties and opportunities presented by their times and circumstances, then what is appropriate here…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
未必宜於彼得其一而未得其二非善論
事者也人之處事無定苟不究其心術之
邪正則暴於顯者或得以掩其微形於外
者未必能保其內非善論人者也知此則
所謂折衷之道夫豈外是也哉請復執事
之間今夫霍去病之無以家為為將之道
得矣而王翦因伐荆之舉顧乃多請田宅
非翦之貪去病之潔也漢武之志狃于征
伐秦王之心過于疑忌故爾然翦之失亦
===
不能無焉盖成敗利鈍非人所能為則亦
何可過為身後之慮也哉申屠嘉之召斬
鄧通為相之道得矣而孔光以丞相之尊
顧乃下拜董賢非嘉之過光之恭也文帝
之優禮相國故嘉得以行其志哀帝之昵
比匪人故光讕之而固其寵耳然嘉之賢
誠不可少焉盖小臣矜寵汙衊王章則將
焉用彼相哉詩書禮樂唯卻縠可晉之彊
縠之力也然能作賦如陸機者乃有河橋

焉用彼相哉詩書禮樂唯郤縠可晉之彊
縠之力也然能作賦如陸機者乃有河橋
punctuated: 未必宜於彼，得其一而未得其二，非善論事者也。人之處事無定，苟不究其心術之邪正，則暴於顯者或得以掩其微，形於外者未必能保其內，非善論人者也。知此，則所謂折衷之道，夫豈外是也哉？請復執事之間。今夫霍去病之無以家為，為將之道得矣；而王翦因伐荆之舉，顧乃多請田宅，非翦之貪、去病之潔也。漢武之志狃于征伐，秦王之心過于疑忌，故爾。然翦之失亦不能無焉，盖成敗利鈍非人所能為，則亦何可過為身後之慮也哉？申屠嘉之召斬鄧通，為相之道得矣；而孔光以丞相之尊，顧乃下拜董賢，非嘉之過、光之恭也。文帝之優禮相國，故嘉得以行其志；哀帝之昵比匪人，故光讕之而固其寵耳。然嘉之賢誠不可少焉，盖小臣矜寵，汙衊王章，則將焉用彼相哉？詩書禮樂，唯卻縠可，晉之彊，縠之力也。然能作賦如陸機者，乃有河橋
translation_en:
…may not necessarily be appropriate in another situation. To grasp one aspect without grasping the other is not to judge affairs well. There is no fixed pattern to how people handle affairs. Unless one investigates whether their motives are corrupt or upright, what is conspicuously displayed may conceal what is obscure, and outward appearances may not reliably attest to what lies within. This is not to judge people well. Once this is understood, how could the so-called way of reaching a balanced judgment lie outside it? Allow me to reply to your question [?].

Now Huo Qubing’s refusal to concern himself with establishing a household accorded with the proper way of a general. Yet Wang Jian, when undertaking the campaign against Jing, repeatedly requested fields and residences. This was not because Wang Jian was avaricious and Huo Qubing incorruptible. It was because Emperor Wu of Han was bent on conquest, whereas the king of Qin was excessively suspicious. Nevertheless, Wang Jian cannot be entirely free of fault. Since success and failure, favorable and unfavorable outcomes, are beyond human control, why should one take excessive thought for what will happen after one’s death?

Shentu Jia’s summoning Deng Tong to have him executed accorded with the proper way of a chief minister. Yet Kong Guang, despite his exalted position as Chief Councilor, bowed low before Dong Xian. This was not because Shentu Jia was overbearing and Kong Guang respectful. Emperor Wen treated his Chief Councilor with exceptional courtesy, so Shentu Jia could carry out his intentions. Emperor Ai associated intimately with unworthy men, so Kong Guang spoke falsely [?] to secure his favor. Nevertheless, Shentu Jia’s worthiness truly must not be slighted. If a petty official flaunts imperial favor and defiles the sovereign’s statutes, what use would there be for such a chief minister?

In the Odes, Documents, rites, and music, only Xi Hu [transcribed 卻縠] was fit for the task; Jin’s strength was due to his efforts. Yet even someone as accomplished in composing rhapsodies as Lu Ji suffered, at Heqiao …

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之敗晉史譏其志不逮言宜矣禮義廉恥
為國四維齊之霸仲之功也然能作論如
柳宗元者乃有伾文之附韓愈譏其僥倖
速進當矣蕭何卒而曹參相蓋大臣薦舉
之公而何舊隙之有張耳王而陳餘戮蓋
小人勢利之交而何舊德之云張安世之
事君以謹厚聞李泌之事君以謀畧著鈞
之為賢相也然薦人而却其謝履道而懼
于盈優于好談神仙詭怪為世所輕者多
===
矣陳萬年之教子以諂韋長孺之遺子以
經其優劣不待言矣然萬年廉平內行甚
脩咸亦言事抗直刺譏近臣蓋亦或有足
取者而非專於諂也公孫弘以布被而取
譏祭遵以布被而見美一為相而矯詐一
為將而儒雅弘何敢望遵乎趙廣漢善為
鉤距而得事情裴延齡廣為鉤距而固君
寵一猶能以民為念一獨知以己為念延
齡豈廣漢之儔乎李賀以父名晉肅故不

punctuated:
之敗，晉史譏其志不逮言，宜矣。禮義廉恥，為國四維，齊之霸，仲之功也。然能作論如柳宗元者，乃有伾文之附，韓愈譏其僥倖速進，當矣。
蕭何卒而曹參相，蓋大臣薦舉之公，而何舊隙之有？張耳王而陳餘戮，蓋小人勢利之交，而何舊德之云？
張安世之事君以謹厚聞，李泌之事君以謀畧著，鈞之為賢相也。然薦人而却其謝，履道而懼于盈，優于好談神仙詭怪、為世所輕者多矣。
陳萬年之教子以諂，韋長孺之遺子以經，其優劣不待言矣。然萬年廉平，內行甚脩，咸亦言事抗直，刺譏近臣，蓋亦或有足取者，而非專於諂也。
公孫弘以布被而取譏，祭遵以布被而見美，一為相而矯詐，一為將而儒雅，弘何敢望遵乎？趙廣漢善為鉤距而得事情，裴延齡廣為鉤距而固君寵，一猶能以民為念，一獨知以己為念，延齡豈廣漢之儔乎？
李賀以父名晉肅，故不
translation_en:
…the defeat at Heqiao. The History of the Jin criticized him for having aspirations that fell short of his words; this was justified. Ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame are the four binding cords of a state; Qi’s hegemony was Guan Zhong’s achievement. Yet even Liu Zongyuan, who could write discourses so well, attached himself to Wang Pi and Wang Shuwen. Han Yu was right to criticize his seeking rapid advancement through opportunism.
When Xiao He died, Cao Can became chancellor: such was the impartiality of a great minister’s recommendation. What place was there for their old enmity? Zhang Er became a king, while Chen Yu was put to death: theirs was the petty man’s friendship founded on power and profit. What was there to say of former kindnesses?
Zhang Anshi was known for his caution and generosity in serving his ruler, and Li Mi for his strategic planning; both were worthy chancellors. Yet the man who recommended others but declined their thanks, followed the Way, and feared the fullness of success was far superior to the one who delighted in talking of immortals and strange marvels and was therefore held in little esteem by the world.
Chen Wannian taught his son flattery, while Wei Changru left his son the Classics. Which was superior needs no explanation. Yet Wannian was honest and impartial, and his private conduct was highly cultivated. His son Xian, too, spoke forthrightly on affairs and criticized the ruler’s close attendants. They thus had some qualities worth commending and did not devote themselves solely to flattery.
Gongsun Hong drew criticism for using a plain cloth quilt, while Ji Zun was praised for doing so. The one was a chancellor who practiced deception; the other was a general of scholarly refinement. How could Hong dare hope to equal Zun? Zhao Guanghan skillfully used probing interrogation to discover the facts of affairs, while Pei Yanling employed such methods extensively to secure the ruler’s favor. The one could still keep the people in mind; the other knew only how to think of himself. How could Yanling be Guanghan’s equal?
Because his father’s name was Jinsu, Li He did not…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
舉進士桑維翰以主司惡其姓而卒不改
業二子之見審矣然賀以少年英銳之資
而所志若彼君子嘉之崔隱甫不欲見牛
仙客韓昌黎三上宰相書二子之心異矣
然愈以平生山斗之望而所為若茲君子
羞之蕭何從高祖而獨收圖籍房玄齡從
秦王而獨收人物盖非圖籍則無以知天
下阨塞戶口疆弱之處非人物則無以為
平定海內之資要之何知天下之勢玄齡
===
其知天下之本乎衛青威震朝廷汲黯獨
違衆而長揖司馬昭位極人臣荀顗獨違
衆而下拜盖揖之所以明折其驕踞之勢
拜之所以陰示其諂屈之心要之黯守人
臣之節顗其姦人之雄乎不從三國之言
而俾齊堅守者路中大夫也不聽楚子之
令而俾宋不下者解楊也其忠不亦同乎
然佯從之以餌敵國不若不從之為全也
卻金以杜故人之請者楊震也縣魚以章

punctuated: 舉進士，桑維翰以主司惡其姓而卒不改業。二子之見審矣，然賀以少年英銳之資，而所志若彼，君子嘉之。崔隱甫不欲見牛仙客，韓昌黎三上宰相書。二子之心異矣，然愈以平生山斗之望，而所為若茲，君子羞之。蕭何從高祖而獨收圖籍，房玄齡從秦王而獨收人物。盖非圖籍則無以知天下阨塞、戶口、疆弱之處，非人物則無以為平定海內之資。要之，何知天下之勢，玄齡其知天下之本乎？衛青威震朝廷，汲黯獨違衆而長揖；司馬昭位極人臣，荀顗獨違衆而下拜。盖揖之所以明折其驕踞之勢，拜之所以陰示其諂屈之心。要之，黯守人臣之節，顗其姦人之雄乎？不從三國之言而俾齊堅守者，路中大夫也；不聽楚子之令而俾宋不下者，解楊也。其忠不亦同乎？然佯從之以餌敵國，不若不從之為全也。卻金以杜故人之請者，楊震也；縣魚以章
translation_en:
…sit for the jinshi examination, while Sang Weihan, though the presiding examiner disliked his surname, ultimately refused to abandon his pursuit. Both men had considered judgments. Yet Li He, endowed with the brilliant promise of youth, set his aspirations as he did, and the gentleman commends him.

Cui Yinfu would not meet Niu Xianke, whereas Han Changli (Han Yu) three times submitted letters to the chief councilor. Their intentions differed. Yet Han Yu, with his lifelong reputation as a figure as revered as Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper, acted thus, and the gentleman feels shame for him.

When Xiao He followed Gaozu, he alone gathered maps and registers; when Fang Xuanling followed the Prince of Qin, he alone gathered talented men. Without maps and registers, there was no way to know the empire’s strategic passes, population, and areas of strength and weakness; without talented men, there were no resources with which to pacify the realm. In sum, Xiao He understood the empire’s strategic circumstances; did Xuanling perhaps understand its foundations?

Wei Qing’s might awed the court, but Ji An alone went against the crowd and offered a deep bow with clasped hands. Sima Zhao attained the highest position a subject could hold, but Xun Yi alone went against the crowd and prostrated himself. The bow openly checked the former’s arrogant bearing; the prostration covertly revealed the latter’s own servile, flattering disposition. In sum, Ji An maintained the integrity proper to a subject; was Xun Yi perhaps a foremost figure among the unscrupulous?

It was Lu Zhongdafu [?] who refused to follow the instructions of the three states and urged Qi to hold firm; it was Jie Yang who disregarded the command of the ruler of Chu and urged Song not to surrender. Was their loyalty not the same? Yet feigning compliance in order to bait an enemy state was less uncompromising than refusing outright.

It was Yang Zhen who rejected gold to forestall an old acquaintance’s request; as for hanging up a fish to make manifest…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
府丞之餽者羊續也其廉不亦同乎然而
受之以愧寮友不若不受之為高也郭子
儀之見回紇薛仁貴之見突厥苟非吾之
恩信素有以結其心吾之兵威素有以奪
其氣則亦安得不如或者之所慮也哉史
臣之稱許是矣馮奉世之破莎車甘陳之
誅郅支大抵皆乘危徼幸之謀而非中國
之利啓釁招禍之漸而生夷狄之心則亦
安得不如議者之所云也哉劉向輩之論

詐冒之爭舉一以例其餘則亦何寃之有
子產治鄭國而民不能欺子賤治單父而
民不忍欺傳之所稱豈無謂乎夷攷其政
一則仁而且明一則清靜無欲執此以臨

尹之所以任天下之重蓋如此而唐臣周

…it was Yang Xu who displayed the gift from the Assistant Prefect. Was their incorruptibility not alike? Yet accepting it in order to shame a fellow official was less lofty than refusing it altogether. When Guo Ziyi met the Huihe and Xue Rengui met the Tujue, had their kindness and trustworthiness not long since won those peoples’ allegiance, and their military might not long since overawed them, how could matters have failed to turn out as some feared? The official historians were right to praise them.

Feng Fengshi’s defeat of Shache and Gan and Chen’s execution of Zhizhi were, on the whole, ventures that courted danger in the hope of a lucky success, rather than benefiting the Central States. They were the beginnings of provocations that invited disaster and stirred ambitions among the foreign peoples. How, then, could matters have failed to turn out as the critics said? The arguments and proposals of Liu Xiang and his fellows were mistaken.

When Zhang Shizhi served as Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, there were no unjustly treated people in the realm; when Dai Zhou served in the Court of Judicial Review, there were no unjust criminal cases in the realm. Surely the historians’ praise rested on some insight? If we examine their times impartially—for example, the deliberation over the violation of the imperial procession’s restrictions at Wei Bridge, or the dispute over fraudulent claims by candidates for office—and take one case as an indication of the rest, what injustice could there have been?

When Zichan governed the state of Zheng, the people could not deceive him; when Zijian governed Shanfu, the people could not bear to deceive him. Surely these statements in the historical accounts had a basis? If we examine their government impartially, the one was humane and discerning, while the other was tranquil and free of desires. Governing their people with these qualities, how could they have been deceived?

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
墀乃以堯舜美文宗於乎文宗豈堯舜之
匹哉墀之諛甚矣人主不當觀史褚遂良
之所以對太宗之言盖如此而異時房玄
齡乃錄而上之於乎史豈人主之所宜觀
者哉玄齡之罪大矣此愚所謂論事當攷
其時勢之難易論人當究其心術之邪正
者盖以此也此亦執事之所謂折衷之道
者也雖然是二者又有本焉窮理是已盖
天下之理散于事天下之事原于理苟理
===
有未窮則凡事之來紛紜迷繆卒無一定
之歸而又奚足以知人也哉管見如此未
知是否惟執事進而教之
第四問
程然
同考試官教諭趙批守令親民固宜慎選然
任法既久得人為難不專倚之考課而兼行久任之
法區處有方不迂不畧此策亦庶幾有裨於
今日乎經生而能留意世務固當為得人慶矣

第四問

程然

同考試官教諭趙批：守令親民，固宜慎選。然任法既久，得人為難，不專倚之考課，而兼行久任之法，區處有方，不迂不畧。此策亦庶幾有裨於今日乎？經生而能留意世務，固當為得人慶矣。
translation_en:
…Chi nevertheless praised Emperor Wenzong by comparing him to Yao and Shun. Alas! Could Wenzong possibly have been the equal of Yao and Shun? Zhou Chi’s flattery was excessive indeed! A ruler ought not to read the historical record: such was the substance of Chu Suiliang’s reply to Emperor Taizong. Yet on another occasion Fang Xuanling copied it out and submitted it to him. Alas! Is the historical record something a ruler ought to read? Great indeed was Xuanling’s fault! This is why I humbly maintain that, when discussing events, one should examine the difficulties and advantages of their historical circumstances, and when judging people, one should investigate whether their intentions were upright or crooked. This, too, is what you call the way of reaching a balanced judgment. Yet these two approaches have a further foundation: the exhaustive investigation of principle. The principles of the world are dispersed among its affairs, and the affairs of the world originate in principle. If any principle remains insufficiently investigated, then as affairs arise, confusion and error will prevent one from ever reaching a settled judgment. How, then, could one adequately understand people? Such is my limited view; I do not know whether it is correct. I ask you to favor me with further instruction.

Fourth Question

Cheng Ran

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: Prefects and county magistrates work closely with the people and certainly ought to be carefully selected. Yet reliance on regulations has long prevailed, and finding suitable men is difficult. Rather than relying exclusively on performance evaluations, this essay also proposes implementing a system of extended tenure. Its arrangements are well conceived, neither impractical nor cursory. Might this policy essay indeed be of some benefit to our own day? That a student of the Classics can attend to the affairs of the world is surely cause to celebrate having found a worthy man.

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官左諭德温批考課當嚴而倚之不專久任
當行而行之不驟論時務而得通融之術主司固為
子拭目也
考試官侍講學士李批久任守令士子固有及之者
至于守令之難與夫考課之不足倚則此對言之詳
矣噫子豈不識天下事者邪
對設官以為民也課功以為官也而實以
為民也夫官為民而立又為民而課試焉
固宜其無不愛民之官無不可行之課試
===
其或不盡然者是必有所以然之故矣今
夫以一郡一邑之民而寄之於人牧猶以
牛羊之羣寄於受牧之人也求牧與芻而
不得將反諸其人歟抑亦立而視其死歟
天下之民望於羣牧如父母然飢寒困踣
賦役囂訟苟可以告之父母者即赴愬於
有司故非豈弟樂易敏銳通達者未可輕
授非真知子民之義者未必能稱守令之
任也我

Comment by Examiner Wen, Left Mentor: Performance evaluations should be rigorous, but should not be relied upon exclusively; extended tenure should be introduced, but not abruptly. In discussing current affairs, you have found a method of flexible accommodation. As chief examiner, I certainly look forward with fresh expectations to what you will accomplish.

Comment by Examiner Li, Academician Expositor-in-Waiting: Other candidates have indeed touched upon extended tenure for prefects and magistrates. But this answer explains in detail both the difficulties of serving as a prefect or magistrate and the inadequacy of relying on performance evaluations. Ah! Can you be someone who does not understand the affairs of the realm?

Response: Offices are established for the people. Achievements are assessed for the sake of officials, yet in truth this too is for the people. Since offices are established for the people, and officials are also examined and evaluated for the people, there should surely be no official who does not cherish the people, and no system of evaluation that cannot be put into practice. If this is not entirely so, there must be reasons why.

To entrust the people of a prefecture or county to a shepherd of men is like entrusting a herd of cattle and sheep to someone charged with tending them. If pasture and fodder are sought but cannot be obtained, should one turn back to that person and hold him responsible, or simply stand by and watch the animals die? The people throughout the realm look to their shepherds as to parents. Whether suffering hunger, cold, hardship, and collapse, or troubles involving taxes, labor service, disputes, and litigation, whenever a matter is one they could report to their parents, they go to the responsible officials to lodge their complaints. Thus such offices must not lightly be conferred upon anyone who is not kindly and approachable, alert and perceptive, and broadly discerning. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
國家重守令之選率取諸科目之傑其才有
小大其歷世有淺深其資性有迂速其喜
好有内外輕重之不同者必擇焉其郡邑
有南北燥濕其風俗有剛柔強弱之異劑
者必擇焉因人而授因地而官使之一志
畢力以福斯民意至渥也故被兹選者既
欲副科目之名之榮人欲稱守令之責之
重其肯偷惰委靡自取課殿也哉
國家考課之法行於貴近者既嚴而於外守
===
令之遠者尤備郡守古諸侯也觀察者一
不滿意即劾去之矣縣令有不待言者故
考課之法主之銓衡主之内臺參之觀察
而又博訪於士論疇咨於數嵗之升達
覲廷之敷奏而其議始定其偷惰委靡法當
速去者不與焉則其法固得於黜陟幽明
之意為多而豈若京房劉邵之煩碎晉魏
唐宋之失實哉夫守令既責之重考之嚴
而其人又自欲勉副

國家考課之法，行於貴近者既嚴，而於外守令之遠者尤備。郡守，古諸侯也，觀察者一不滿意，即劾去之矣，縣令有不待言者。故考課之法，主之銓衡，主之内臺，參之觀察，而又博訪於士論，疇咨於數嵗之升達、覲廷之敷奏，而其議始定。其偷惰委靡、法當速去者，不與焉。則其法固得於黜陟幽明之意為多，而豈若京房、劉邵之煩碎，晉、魏、唐、宋之失實哉？夫守令既責之重，考之嚴，而其人又自欲勉副

…the state attaches great importance to selecting prefects and magistrates, generally choosing the outstanding men produced by the examinations. Their abilities vary in scope, their experience of the world in depth, and their natural dispositions in deliberateness or quickness; their preferences differ as to inner and outer concerns and relative importance. These distinctions must be weighed in selecting them. Prefectures and counties differ in being northern or southern, dry or damp, and their customs differ in their mixture [?] of firmness and gentleness, strength and weakness. These distinctions, too, must be weighed. Appointments are made according to the person, and offices assigned according to the locality, so that officials may concentrate their purpose and expend all their strength on benefiting the people. The intention is most generous. Thus, those selected wish both to live up to the honor of their examination distinction and, each of them [?], to discharge the weighty responsibilities of prefects and magistrates. Would they willingly become idle and dispirited, bringing upon themselves the lowest assessment?
The state's system of performance evaluation is already strict toward eminent officials close to the throne, and is still more comprehensive for prefects and magistrates serving far away in the provinces. A prefect occupies the position of an ancient regional lord; yet if an inspecting official is in any way dissatisfied with him, he is immediately impeached and removed. The case of county magistrates goes without saying. Thus, performance evaluation is directed by the Ministry of Personnel and by the Censorate, with inspecting officials participating. Moreover, opinion among the scholars is widely canvassed, and consultations draw upon reports submitted over several years [?] and statements presented at court audiences; only then is the assessment settled. Those who are idle and dispirited and who, under the regulations, ought to be removed promptly are excluded from this procedure. This system therefore substantially realizes the intent of demoting the benighted and promoting the enlightened. How could it resemble the excessive minutiae of Jing Fang and Liu Shao, or the failure to reflect actual performance under the Jin, Wei, Tang, and Song? Now, prefects and magistrates are charged with weighty responsibilities and evaluated strictly, while they themselves also wish to strive to meet…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
意不為偷惰委靡之習固宜其百姓富庶政
平訟理者而今之民日益窮訟日益繁轉
徙流亡者日益眾近自
畿輔重地已有然者他藩可知矣是獨無其
故哉愚不識天下事竊謂乆任之法不行
也孔子曰善人為邦百年亦可以勝殘去
殺矣又曰苟有用我者朞月而已可也三
年有成子產為政累年而後化成伯禽治
魯三年而後報政今之人未必皆聖賢也
===
聰明得於簡冊之緒言志力奪於舉業之
舊習一旦寄以民牧之任上而監臨觀察
責其成下而府史胥徒伺其隙其奮翼策
步不安小成者必一二年治乃有緒焉彼
方有治緒可尋也而旁郡別邑已有遷陟
內拜者矣於是而速進之念生速進之念
生則為民之意短而求上之意急謀身之
術巧而取民之計多百姓固何利於是哉
下之人知其意欲速也吏胥得以肆其謾

平訟理者而今之民日益窮訟日益繁轉
徙流亾者日益衆近自
畿輔重地巳有然者他藩可知矣是獨無其
故哉愚不識天下事竊謂久任之法不行
也孔子曰善人為邦百年亦可以勝殘去
殺矣又曰苟有用我者朞月而巳可也三
年有成子產為政累年而後化成伯禽治
魯三年而後報政今之人未必皆聖賢也
===
聰明得於簡冊之緒言志力奪於舉業之
舊習一旦寄以民牧之任上而監臨觀察
責其成下而府史胥徒伺其隙其奮翼策
步不安小成者必一二年治乃有緒焉彼
方有治緒可尋也而旁郡別邑巳有遷陟
内拜者矣於是而速進之念生速進之念
生則為民之意短而求上之意急謀身之
術巧而取民之計多百姓固何利於是哉
下之人知其意欲速也吏胥得以肆其譏
punctuated: 意，不為偷惰委靡之習，固宜其百姓富庶，政平訟理者，而今之民日益窮，訟日益繁，轉徙流亡者日益眾。近自畿輔重地已有然者，他藩可知矣。是獨無其故哉？愚不識天下事，竊謂乆任之法不行也。孔子曰：「善人為邦百年，亦可以勝殘去殺矣。」又曰：「苟有用我者，朞月而已可也，三年有成。」子產為政，累年而後化成；伯禽治魯，三年而後報政。今之人未必皆聖賢也，聰明得於簡冊之緒言，志力奪於舉業之舊習。一旦寄以民牧之任，上而監臨觀察責其成，下而府史胥徒伺其隙，其奮翼策步、不安小成者，必一二年治乃有緒焉。彼方有治緒可尋也，而旁郡別邑已有遷陟內拜者矣。於是而速進之念生。速進之念生，則為民之意短，而求上之意急；謀身之術巧，而取民之計多。百姓固何利於是哉？下之人知其意欲速也，吏胥得以肆其謾……
translation_en:
…the expectations placed upon them, and avoid habits of indolence and listlessness. Surely their people ought therefore to prosper and multiply, their government to be equitable, and their lawsuits properly adjudicated. Yet today the people grow poorer by the day, lawsuits become ever more numerous, and increasing numbers wander from place to place or flee their homes. Such conditions already exist close at hand, in the vital metropolitan region; what things must be like in the other provinces can readily be inferred. Can this alone be without a cause? Though I am ignorant of the affairs of the realm, I venture to suggest that it is because the policy of keeping officials long in their posts is not practiced.

Confucius said, “If good men governed a state for a hundred years, they could overcome cruelty and dispense with executions.” He also said, “If someone were to employ me, something could be done within a full year; in three years there would be accomplishments.” Zichan governed for several years before his transforming influence took full effect; Boqin governed Lu for three years before reporting on his administration. The men of today are not necessarily all sages or worthies. Their understanding comes from scraps of sayings in books, while their resolve and energy are sapped by ingrained habits of examination study. Once entrusted with responsibility as shepherds of the people, they face supervisory and inspecting officials above who demand results, and clerks and underlings below who watch for their weaknesses. Even those who spread their wings, spur themselves onward, and refuse to rest content with small accomplishments must take a year or two before their administration begins to take shape.

Just when their administration has begun to show discernible results, officials in neighboring prefectures and other counties have already won promotion or appointment to the central government. Thus arises the desire for rapid advancement. Once that desire arises, their concern for the people diminishes, while their eagerness to seek favor above intensifies; their techniques for advancing their own interests become more ingenious, and their schemes for extracting wealth from the people multiply. What benefit can the common people possibly derive from this? Those below know that they are eager to advance quickly, and the clerks and underlings can give free rein to their deceit…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
豪猾得以窺其弊上下之間一切苟且而
已錐考課日嚴賞罰日加彼速進者固不
俟是而已有岐路可郷矣其不畏刺舉者
又或中有所倚焉如是則信有如杜子恕
所謂歷代累聖而考績之法不著課試之
要未立也蘇軾曰有官必有課有課必有
賞罰有官無課是無官也有課無賞罰是
無課也天下之吏不可勝考必刺舉於其
所屬之長而賞罰得以加焉其意以為守
===
令之賢否考於職司而於御史臺別立一
司中丞舉其綱屬官之強明者治其事彼
蘇軾固為宋言也今始於觀察升於銓衡
內臺內臺銓衡又第其品而黜陟於其
上此亦軾之意而益加詳者也夫久任之意不
堅而專倚之考課則所課者時日之近効
而其所以為最者又或得於悅上偽增之
私當道者亦何所按哉其拙於逢迎篤意
撫字而上不之知者又非考課之所能得

而其所以爲最者又或得於悅上僞增之

punctuated: 豪猾得以窺其弊，上下之間，一切苟且而已。錐考課日嚴，賞罰日加，彼速進者固不俟是，而已有岐路可郷矣。其不畏刺舉者，又或中有所倚焉。如是，則信有如杜子恕所謂歷代累聖，而考績之法不著，課試之要未立也。蘇軾曰：「有官必有課，有課必有賞罰。有官無課，是無官也；有課無賞罰，是無課也。天下之吏不可勝考，必刺舉於其所屬之長，而賞罰得以加焉。」其意以為守令之賢否，考於職司，而於御史臺別立一司，中丞舉其綱，屬官之強明者治其事。彼蘇軾固為宋言也。今始於觀察，升於銓衡、內臺，內臺、銓衡又第其品，而黜陟於其上。此亦軾之意，而益加詳者也。夫久任之意不堅，而專倚之考課，則所課者時日之近効，而其所以為最者，又或得於悅上偽增之私，當道者亦何所按哉？其拙於逢迎，篤意撫字，而上不之知者，又非考課之所能得
translation_en:
…and powerful, unscrupulous men can exploit their failings. Between superiors and subordinates, everything becomes a matter of expediency. Though [?] performance evaluations grow stricter by the day and rewards and punishments are increasingly applied, those seeking rapid advancement need not wait for these: they already have alternative paths to pursue. Those who do not fear investigation and impeachment may also have someone within the administration on whom they rely. If so, the situation is indeed as Du Zishu described: through successive dynasties and many sage rulers, methods of evaluating performance have not been made clear, nor have the essentials of assessment been established.

Su Shi said: “Where there is an office, there must be assessment; where there is assessment, there must be reward and punishment. To have offices without assessment is equivalent to having no offices; to have assessment without reward and punishment is equivalent to having no assessment. The officials of the realm are too numerous to examine exhaustively. Their immediate superiors must investigate and impeach them, so that rewards and punishments can be applied.” His intention was that the competence of prefects and magistrates should be assessed by the responsible authorities, and that a separate bureau should be established within the Censorate. The Censor-in-Chief would oversee its general direction, while resolute and discerning subordinate officials would conduct its business. Su Shi was, of course, speaking for the Song dynasty. Today, assessment begins with the surveillance authorities and proceeds upward to the personnel-selection authorities and the central Censorate. The central Censorate and personnel-selection authorities then rank the officials and, from above, demote or promote them. This, too, embodies Su Shi’s intention, but elaborates it further.

Yet if the commitment to keeping officials in their posts for a long term is not firm, and reliance is placed exclusively on performance evaluations, what is assessed will be short-term results. Moreover, the grounds for an outstanding rating may arise from self-serving efforts to please superiors and falsely inflate achievements. What, then, can those in authority use as a basis for scrutiny? Those who are inept at ingratiating themselves, yet sincerely devoted to nurturing the people, and whose superiors do not recognize them, are likewise beyond the ability of performance evaluations to identify…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也夫有志者拜一命之寄亦欲展布以爲
久圖而速進者得以惑其意是使天下無
誠心為民者矣然轉移之機豈一言之所
能悉一日之所能變哉愚請試行之數人
可也盖人之材智器局大畧相同唯有志
者率其力之所不及以趨其志之所欲就
故其受若直也恒勉勉焉惟恐或負則其
所望寧小無大寧卑無崇而其所為也寧
拙無巧寧久無速誠得是人而任之則所
===
謂悃愊無華嵗計有餘者於是而久任焉
秩當遷也不移其地祿當益也不奪其官
過可畧也不拘以文法之細人可諒也不
間以毀譽之言或璽書慰勉以新其意或
就加服命以旌其能若果有效也破格用
之異待之終身焉彼速進者曰吾所進者
在於格之內而彼乃獨超于格之外則彼
之所謂遲者速而吾之所謂速者遲矣故
速不必沮也自有權以遲之不必遍行於

punctuated: 也。夫有志者，拜一命之寄，亦欲展布以爲久圖，而速進者得以惑其意，是使天下無誠心為民者矣。然轉移之機，豈一言之所能悉、一日之所能變哉？愚請試行之數人，可也。盖人之材智器局，大畧相同，唯有志者，率其力之所不及，以趨其志之所欲就。故其受若直也，恒勉勉焉，惟恐或負。則其所望，寧小無大，寧卑無崇；而其所為也，寧拙無巧，寧久無速。誠得是人而任之，則所謂悃愊無華、嵗計有餘者，於是而久任焉。秩當遷也，不移其地；祿當益也，不奪其官；過可畧也，不拘以文法之細；人可諒也，不間以毀譽之言。或璽書慰勉，以新其意；或就加服命，以旌其能。若果有效也，破格用之，異待之終身焉。彼速進者曰：「吾所進者在於格之內，而彼乃獨超于格之外，則彼之所謂遲者速，而吾之所謂速者遲矣。」故速不必沮也，自有權以遲之。不必遍行於
translation_en:
…either. A man of resolve, on receiving even his first official commission, wishes to put his abilities into practice and make lasting plans. Yet those who advance rapidly can unsettle his purpose. This leaves the realm without men sincerely devoted to serving the people. But how could the means of bringing about change be fully explained in a single statement, or the change accomplished in a single day? I humbly propose trying this with a few men.
Men’s talents, intelligence, capacity, and breadth of vision are broadly similar. Only those with resolve press beyond the limits of their strength toward what they aspire to accomplish. Thus, when receiving their remuneration [?], they continually exert themselves, fearing only that they might fail their trust. In their expectations, they prefer little to much and a low position to a lofty one; in their conduct, they prefer plain effort to cleverness and lasting achievement to quick results. If such men can indeed be found and appointed—men of the kind described as “utterly sincere, without show, whose achievements, reckoned over a year, are more than sufficient”—then let them remain long in office. When their rank is due to rise, do not transfer them elsewhere; when their stipend is due to increase, do not remove them from their posts. Where their faults may be overlooked, do not bind them with the minutiae of legal formalities; where the men deserve understanding, do not let words of blame or praise undermine trust in them. At times, send letters bearing the imperial seal to console and encourage them and renew their purpose; at others, confer higher robes and commissions upon them in their present posts to recognize their ability. If they truly produce results, employ them beyond the usual rules and accord them exceptional treatment throughout their lives.
Those who advance rapidly will then say: “My advancement remains within the established rules, while that man alone has risen beyond them. Thus what was called his slow progress is fast, and what was called my fast progress is slow.” There is therefore no need to obstruct rapid advancement: there are discretionary means to slow it. Nor need this be implemented throughout …

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
郡縣而獨行之數人而亦已化矣於乎於
上下相安之時而輒倡以久任之說故必
有駭視改聽不安其位者愚請得以意而
試行之可乎今天下仕者水陸舟車之用
不同遷轉調更其喜好不同彼方與民相
安於北而復任之於南其不願必矣故於
此亦必有調停之法不拂其情而俾彼得
以終其惠此亦久任之意也雖然久任之
事在上不在下在近不在遠唯執事擇焉

郡縣，而獨行之數人，而亦已化矣。於乎！於上下相安之時，而輒倡以久任之說，故必有駭視改聽、不安其位者。愚請得以意而試行之，可乎？今天下仕者，水陸舟車之用不同，遷轉調更，其喜好不同。彼方與民相安於北，而復任之於南，其不願必矣。故於此亦必有調停之法，不拂其情，而俾彼得以終其惠，此亦久任之意也。雖然，久任之事，在上不在下，在近不在遠，唯執事擇焉。

第五問
仲選

同考試官教諭何批：財賦，國家大計也。古人制賦有成法，節財有定論。子能舉以為今日足國裕民之助，而辭意和厚，區處的確，必有用之士也。敬服！敬服！

考試官左諭德温批：用古人意思，處今日時務，一一若出自其口，而讀之不厭者，此對是也。昔有補綴疏草而復以上者，子其得之乎？
translation_en:
…throughout the prefectures and counties; applying it only to a few men would already bring about a transformation. Alas! To advocate long tenure when superiors and subordinates are at ease with one another will surely cause some to look on in alarm, listen with changed attention, and feel insecure in their posts. Might I humbly request that this proposal be tried? Officials throughout the realm differ in their use of boats and carriages for travel by water and land, and their preferences regarding promotion, transfer, and reassignment also differ. If a man is living harmoniously with the people in the north and is then appointed to the south, he will certainly be unwilling to go. Here, too, there must therefore be a means of accommodation, so that his wishes are not thwarted and he can bring his beneficent work to completion. This, too, accords with the purpose of long tenure. Nevertheless, the matter of long tenure rests with those above, not those below; with those near the court, not those far away. I leave the choice to you, sir.

Fifth Policy Question
Second Selection

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: Finance and taxation are a great concern of the state. The ancients had established methods for levying taxes and settled principles for regulating expenditure. You have drawn upon these to help provide sufficient resources for the state and prosperity for the people today. Your language and meaning are measured and generous, and your arrangements precise and sound. You must surely be a man whose abilities will prove useful. I admire you! I admire you!

Comment by Examiner Wen, Left Admonisher: This answer applies the ideas of the ancients to the practical affairs of today, making each point seem to issue from their own mouths, yet never wearying the reader. In former times, there were those who pieced together draft memorials and submitted them anew. Have you perhaps grasped their method?

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍講學士李批理財之道人人知之人人能
言之有考據有斷制有歸宿若此對者蓋亦鮮矣敬
錄以
獻
對天下之計一家之計也天下之財吾與
天下共理之也故上不必益而下不必損
君不必富而民不必貧如家人父子然父
有之將以遺其子也子有之將以致之父
也而後天下之情一而天下之用足百志
===
成而禮俗刑矣古之人所以大過人者理
天下之財而天下不疑其利擅天下之有
而天下不疑其貪家人父子之謂也唐楊
炎言於德宗曰財賦者邦國之大本生人
之喉命天下治亂輕重繫焉而不可忽也
盖自古有天下者未有不善理財而足國
裕民者獨怪夫儒者諱言利而聚斂之臣
廼竊善理財之名卒使民日益窮而用日
益蹙古今之禍可鑒也孔子罕言利而損

translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Li, Expositor-in-Waiting: Everyone knows the principles of managing wealth, and everyone can speak of them. Yet an answer such as this, grounded in evidence, displaying decisive judgment, and reaching a definite conclusion, is surely rare. I respectfully copy it out for presentation.

Reply: Planning for all under Heaven is like planning for a single household. The wealth of all under Heaven is something I administer jointly with all under Heaven. Thus those above need not gain, nor those below lose; the ruler need not grow rich, nor the people grow poor. It is like fathers and sons within a household: what the father possesses, he intends to leave to his son; what the son possesses, he intends to offer to his father. Only then will the sentiments of all under Heaven be united and their resources sufficient, their many aspirations fulfilled, and their rites and customs duly formed. What made the men of antiquity so far surpass others was that they administered the wealth of all under Heaven without anyone suspecting them of seeking profit, and controlled all its possessions without anyone suspecting them of greed. This is what is meant by treating one another as fathers and sons within a household.

Yang Yan of the Tang said to Emperor Dezong: “Revenue is the great foundation of the state, the throat and lifeblood of the people. Order and disorder under Heaven, and the balance between them, depend upon it; it cannot be neglected.” Indeed, from antiquity, none who ruled all under Heaven has ever made the state sufficiently provisioned and the people prosperous without managing wealth well. What is especially strange is that Confucian scholars shrink from speaking of profit, while officials who exact wealth from the people usurp the reputation of being skilled financial administrators. In the end, they make the people poorer by the day and resources for expenditure ever more constrained. Such calamities, ancient and modern, offer a warning. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上益下自易發之孟子不言利曰無政事
則財用不足大學生財之道固即周官理
財之道也周官理財之道固即利用厚生
之說也聖賢何嘗不理財乎為民理之為
天下理之而不為巳也嘗考周官以九賦
斂財賄以九式均節財用以九貢致邦國
之用冢宰制其出司徒制其入其出也固
以稽其入也其入也固以稽其出也上無
侈心下無蔽奸法莫有善於此者彼安石
===
何人迺欲倣之而行新法其意不過為人
主斂財耳然卒以之而禍國家盖非周官
之過用之者之過也彼周官未作之前禹
貢任土作貢田賦什而稅一公田藉而不
稅制用必於歲杪夏殷之制可考也周官
既作之後一變而為春秋再變而為戰國
理財之法雖不可得而詳而有若對哀公
之數語孟子與齊梁君之問答而其時可
知矣秦孝公開阡陌盡地力至始皇而其

translation_en:
…those above and benefiting those below: this principle is set forth in the Book of Changes. Mengzi did not speak of profit, yet said: “Without proper government, financial resources will be insufficient.” The way of producing wealth in the Great Learning is precisely the way of managing wealth in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan); the way of managing wealth in the Offices of Zhou is precisely the teaching of making resources useful and enriching the people’s livelihood. When have sages and worthies ever failed to manage wealth? They manage it for the people and for all under Heaven, not for themselves. I have examined the Offices of Zhou: the nine levies collect wealth and goods; the nine expenditure standards regulate and economize the use of resources; and the nine forms of tribute supply what is needed from the regional states. The Minister of State controls expenditure, and the Minister of Education controls revenue. Expenditure is assessed against revenue, and revenue against expenditure. Those above have no extravagant desires, and those below conceal no wrongdoing. No system could be better than this. Who was that Anshi, that he should presume to imitate it and institute his New Policies? His intention was merely to gather wealth for the ruler, yet in the end he brought disaster upon the state through them. This was not the fault of the Offices of Zhou, but of the person who applied it.
Before the Offices of Zhou was composed, the Tribute of Yu prescribed tribute according to the land’s capacities. The land levy took one part in ten; public fields were cultivated through obligatory labor rather than taxed; and expenditure was invariably determined at the year’s end. The institutions of the Xia and Yin can thus be traced. After the Offices of Zhou was composed, one transformation brought the Spring and Autumn period, and another the Warring States period. Although the methods of managing wealth cannot be known in detail, the few remarks You Ruo addressed to Duke Ai, together with Mengzi’s exchanges with the rulers of Qi and Liang, allow us to understand those times. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
賦益重盖二十倍於周矣漢懲秦弊田租
什五而稅一加以高惠之寬仁文景之恭
儉固宜有錢朽而不可校粟腐而不可食
矣奈之何武帝好大喜功有以盡耗之哉
隋文帝躬脩節儉益免田租至煬帝而賦
役繁重百姓始不勝怨矣唐承隋後口分
世業租庸調之法府衛兵之制無不善者
永淳以後賦役並起又繼以天寶之驕奢
如之何其不壞哉宋之理財也版部有左
===
計有右計有總計其後三司有使度支有
使磨勘有司會計有錄祥符天禧之時可
謂盛矣然一壞於煕寧君臣之變更再壞
於紹興以後之妄費而用不可支矣抑愚
嘗有考焉三代授人以田而未有戶賦兩
漢不授人以田而輕其戶賦魏至唐中葉
則因授田之名而重其戶賦至宋煕寧以
後則日新月盛賦日益增而民日益困國
日益危矣其間喜事之臣如王鉷有嵗進

賦益重，盖二十倍於周矣。漢懲秦弊，田租什五而稅一，加以高惠之寬仁、文景之恭儉，固宜有錢朽而不可校、粟腐而不可食矣。奈之何武帝好大喜功，有以盡耗之哉！隋文帝躬脩節儉，益免田租，至煬帝而賦役繁重，百姓始不勝怨矣。唐承隋後，口分、世業、租庸調之法，府衛兵之制，無不善者。永淳以後，賦役並起，又繼以天寶之驕奢，如之何其不壞哉！宋之理財也，版部有左計，有右計，有總計。其後三司有使，度支有使，磨勘有司，會計有錄，祥符、天禧之時，可謂盛矣。然一壞於煕寧君臣之變更，再壞於紹興以後之妄費，而用不可支矣。
抑愚嘗有考焉：三代授人以田，而未有戶賦；兩漢不授人以田，而輕其戶賦；魏至唐中葉，則因授田之名而重其戶賦；至宋煕寧以後，則日新月盛，賦日益增，而民日益困，國日益危矣。其間喜事之臣，如王鉷有嵗進
translation_en:
…taxation grew still heavier, reaching perhaps twenty times that of the Zhou. Taking warning from the abuses of the Qin, the Han levied a land tax of one part in fifteen. Added to this were the generosity and benevolence of Emperors Gaozu and Hui, and the modesty and frugality of Emperors Wen and Jing. It was certainly fitting that money should accumulate until its strings rotted and it could no longer be counted, and grain until it spoiled and could no longer be eaten. How could Emperor Wu, with his fondness for grand undertakings and military achievements, have exhausted it all!
Emperor Wen of the Sui personally practiced frugality and granted further remissions of land tax. By the time of Emperor Yang, however, taxes and labor services had become onerous, and the common people could no longer contain their resentment. The Tang succeeded the Sui. Its regulations for individually allotted and hereditary fields, its system of grain tax, labor service, and payment in textiles, and its system of garrison and guard troops were all sound. After the Yongchun era, taxes and labor obligations increased together; these were followed by the arrogance and extravagance of the Tianbao era. How could the system have failed to collapse!
In the Song administration of finance, the revenue ministry had a Left Accounts Section, a Right Accounts Section, and a General Accounts Section. Subsequently, there were commissioners for the Three Fiscal Agencies and for the Tax Bureau, offices for auditing, and records of fiscal accounts. In the Xiangfu and Tianxi eras, this could be called a flourishing system. Yet it was first undermined by the changes made by the ruler and his ministers during the Xining era, and undermined again by reckless expenditure from the Shaoxing era onward, until expenses could no longer be met.
Now I, in my humble judgment, have investigated this matter. The Three Dynasties allotted fields to the people and had no household tax. The two Han dynasties did not allot fields to the people but kept their household taxes light. From the Wei to the middle of the Tang, the pretext of allotting fields was used to impose heavier household taxes. From the Song’s Xining era onward, new exactions appeared daily and multiplied monthly: taxes increased day by day, the people became increasingly impoverished, and the state increasingly imperiled. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
韋皐有日進李兼有月進裴肅有刺史
進蕭綬有判官之進盖唐元宗德宗方只
意於聚財故鉷皐兼肅之徒得以利而誘
之其後兵革繼起禍亂相仍朱泚之難竟
不能以內藏而助一錐有瓊林大盈之積
何益哉宋亦有之封椿庫置於太祖景福
庫置於太宗其後神宗又更景福庫名自
製詩以揭之是亦內藏也然軍興賞賚則
用之水旱災傷則用之三司用乏則助之
===
諸路用乏則助之宋太祖嘗曰俟錢滿五
百萬緡當問契丹贖幽薊又曰用絹二十
疋募一胡人首其意如此是非若唐人之
私用矣然以愚言之天子者有天下際天
薄海莫非已有而又何必以內藏為哉惟
其目為內藏也宰相不得以式貢均節其
出入版曹不得以簿書勾考其在亡本為
燕私之奉日消月耗而自奉亦不足矣蓋
人君之於天下廣取以給用莫若節用而

punctuated:
韋皐有日進，李兼有月進，裴肅有刺史進，蕭綬有判官之進。盖唐元宗、德宗方只意於聚財，故鉷、皐、兼、肅之徒得以利而誘之。其後兵革繼起，禍亂相仍，朱泚之難，竟不能以內藏而助一錐，有瓊林、大盈之積何益哉？
宋亦有之：封椿庫置於太祖，景福庫置於太宗。其後神宗又更景福庫名，自製詩以揭之，是亦內藏也。然軍興賞賚則用之，水旱災傷則用之，三司用乏則助之，諸路用乏則助之。宋太祖嘗曰：「俟錢滿五百萬緡，當問契丹贖幽薊。」又曰：「用絹二十疋募一胡人首。」其意如此，是非若唐人之私用矣。
然以愚言之，天子者有天下，際天薄海，莫非已有，而又何必以內藏為哉？惟其目為內藏也，宰相不得以式貢均節其出入，版曹不得以簿書勾考其在亡。本為燕私之奉，日消月耗，而自奉亦不足矣。蓋人君之於天下，廣取以給用，莫若節用而
translation_en:
…Wei Gao made daily offerings, Li Jian monthly offerings, Pei Su offerings as prefect, and Xiao Shou offerings as administrative assistant. Since Emperors Yuanzong and Dezong of Tang were then intent solely on amassing wealth, men such as Wang Hong, Wei Gao, Li Jian, and Pei Su could entice them with profit. Thereafter, warfare broke out repeatedly, and calamity followed turmoil. During Zhu Ci’s rebellion, the palace treasury ultimately could not provide even an awl’s worth of assistance [?]. What benefit, then, were the reserves in the Qionglin and Daying treasuries?
The Song also had such institutions: the Fengchun Treasury was established under Taizu, and the Jingfu Treasury under Taizong. Later, Shenzong renamed the Jingfu Treasury and composed a poem himself to display there. These too were palace treasuries. Yet their funds were used for rewards when armies were mobilized and for relief when floods or droughts caused devastation. When the State Finance Commission lacked funds, they supplied assistance; when the various circuits lacked funds, they likewise supplied assistance. Emperor Taizu of Song once said: “When the money reaches five million strings of cash, I shall ask the Khitan about redeeming You and Ji.” He also said: “Offer twenty bolts of silk as a bounty for each head of a Hu tribesman.” Such were his intentions: this was unlike the private expenditure of the Tang rulers.
Yet in my humble view, the Son of Heaven possesses all under Heaven. Everything extending to the bounds of the sky and the shores of the seas belongs to him; why, then, must he maintain a palace treasury? Precisely because it is designated a palace treasury, the grand councilors cannot regulate its receipts and expenditures according to the prescribed tribute provisions, nor can the Ministry of Revenue use its account books to audit what remains and what is missing. Originally intended to support the ruler’s private pleasures, its resources dwindle day by day and month by month, until they no longer suffice even for his own expenses. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
取廉譬之小民之家方其平時所望不過
十金計其衣食妻子之費出入於十金之
中而亦已足矣及其稍富也意之所欲者
日以漸廣所入日益衆所欲日益不足不
知罪其用之不節而獨以為求之未至也
是以富而愈奢奢而愈貧嗚呼此愚所謂
天下之計一家之計也天下之財吾與天
下共理之而已善乎蘇軾之言曰為國有
三計三年耕必有一年之蓄以三十年之
===
通計可以九年而無飢歲之所入足用而
有餘是以九年之蓄常閒而無用此萬世
之計也其不能者一歲之入纔足以供一
歲之出天下之産僅足以供天下之用此
一時之計也其最下者量出以為入用之
不給取之益多天下晏然無大患難而盡
用衰世苟且之法不知有急何以加之此
不終月之計也以愚言之自古人君何嘗
不欲為萬世之計哉自井田之法壞寓兵

取廉。譬之小民之家，方其平時，所望不過十金，計其衣食妻子之費，出入於十金之中，而亦已足矣。及其稍富也，意之所欲者日以漸廣，所入日益衆，所欲日益不足。不知罪其用之不節，而獨以為求之未至也，是以富而愈奢，奢而愈貧。嗚呼！此愚所謂天下之計，一家之計也。天下之財，吾與天下共理之而已。
善乎蘇軾之言曰：「為國有三計：三年耕，必有一年之蓄；以三十年之通計，可以九年而無飢。歲之所入，足用而有餘，是以九年之蓄常閒而無用，此萬世之計也。其不能者，一歲之入纔足以供一歲之出，天下之産僅足以供天下之用，此一時之計也。其最下者，量出以為入，用之不給，取之益多。天下晏然，無大患難，而盡用衰世苟且之法，不知有急，何以加之？此不終月之計也。」以愚言之，自古人君何嘗不欲為萬世之計哉？自井田之法壞，寓兵
translation_en:
…and exact little. Consider the household of an ordinary person. In normal circumstances, he hopes for no more than ten units of gold. Reckoning the expense of clothing and food for himself, his wife, and his children, he keeps receipts and expenditures within those ten units, and they suffice. Once he becomes somewhat wealthier, however, his desires gradually expand day by day. His income continually increases, yet his desires are ever less satisfied. He does not blame his lack of restraint in spending, but thinks only that he has not gone far enough in seeking income. Thus, the richer he becomes, the more extravagant he grows; and the more extravagant, the poorer. Alas! This is what I mean when I say that managing the resources of the realm is like managing those of a household. The wealth of the realm is simply something I administer together with all under Heaven.
Well said are Su Shi’s words: “There are three plans for managing a state. Three years of cultivation must provide one year’s reserves. Reckoning over thirty years in all, there will be enough to go nine years without hunger. Annual receipts suffice for expenditure and leave a surplus, so the nine years’ reserves always remain untouched and unused. This is a plan for ten thousand generations. For those unable to achieve this, one year’s receipts barely suffice to meet one year’s expenditures, and the realm’s production barely suffices to meet its needs. This is a plan for the moment. The lowest approach is to determine receipts according to expenditures: when resources do not meet spending, ever more is exacted. Though the realm is peaceful and faces no great calamity, all the expedients of a declining age are employed. Should an emergency arise, they do not know how they could exact anything more. This is a plan that will not last out the month.” In my humble view, when have rulers since antiquity ever failed to desire a plan for ten thousand generations? Ever since the well-field system broke down, and the practice of incorporating soldiers…

punctuated: 於農之意失，而養兵之費多矣。自封建之法壊，郡縣天下之制立，而供官之費多矣。况兵養於平時者不可得用，而所費以給之者又非可用之兵；官建於制額者，其禄有常，而所費以給之者率非有制之設。故蘇轍有曰：「方今之計，莫如豐財。非求財而益之也，去其害財者而已：曰冗官也，曰冗兵也，曰冗費也。」朱子有曰：「天下國家之大務，莫大於恤民。恤民之實在省賦，省賦之實在治軍。治軍省賦以為恤民之本，則又在人君正心術以立紀綱。」蓋心術正，紀綱立，則《大學》之生財、《周官》之理財、《大易》損上益下之說，特有天下者治用之一事耳。雖有水旱、盜賊、邊防之擾，又何足為意哉？書生與聞邦國之大計，嫌於出位，唯執事進教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…the principle of embedding soldiers among the farming population was lost, and the expense of maintaining troops increased. Since the system of enfeoffment broke down and a system of governing all under Heaven through prefectures and counties was established, the expense of supporting officials has increased. Moreover, troops maintained in peacetime cannot be put to use, and those on whose support funds are spent are not serviceable soldiers. Officials appointed within the authorized establishment have fixed stipends, yet those on whose support funds are spent generally occupy posts outside that establishment. Thus Su Zhe said: “For present-day policy, nothing is better than making resources abundant. This does not mean seeking wealth and adding to it, but simply eliminating what depletes it: superfluous officials, superfluous troops, and superfluous expenditure.” Master Zhu said: “Among the great affairs of the realm and the state, none is greater than caring for the people. The substance of caring for the people lies in reducing taxation; the substance of reducing taxation lies in putting the military in order. To make military reform and reduced taxation the foundation of caring for the people depends, in turn, on the ruler’s rectifying his mind and intentions so as to establish proper order and discipline.”

For once the ruler’s mind and intentions are rectified and order and discipline established, the generation of wealth discussed in the Great Learning, the management of wealth in the Offices of Zhou, and the teaching of diminishing those above to benefit those below in the Book of Changes are merely one aspect of how the possessor of all under Heaven manages expenditure. Even if there are disturbances from floods, droughts, bandits, or frontier defense, why should they give cause for concern? For a scholar to take part in deliberations on the great plans of the state may seem to overstep his station. I would be most fortunate if you, honored sir, would offer me instruction.

translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

Today, any scholar in the realm who distinguishes himself through talent and accomplishment aspires to selection for office. The instruction given by fathers and teachers, and the talent sought and held in reserve by local communities, likewise often have this as their aim. Our dynasty treats scholars with generous courtesy, and its method of selection is focused on a single course. It is therefore fitting that scholars should be settled in their aspirations and uniform in their practices.

As for methods of selection, the Zhou dynasty entrusted responsibility to local communities, for these were the source of public judgment. Under the Han, responsibility was sometimes assigned to commanderies and kingdoms, ranked marquises, and officials of two-thousand-bushel rank; sometimes to the Three Dukes, the Chamberlain for Attendants, Censors, the Director of Retainers, and Regional Governors. Candidates were recommended under such categories as Flourishing Talent (maocai), Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian), Understanding the Classics (mingjing), and Worthy and Good, Capable of Unreserved Remonstrance (xianliang jijian). By the Sui and Tang, there were also categories for Understanding the Classics and Outstanding…

translation_en: …scholars, metropolitan graduates (jinshi), and the various examinations held by imperial decree. The Song likewise had examinations in elucidating the classics, examinations for metropolitan graduates in poetry and rhapsody, and special examinations by imperial decree. These selections were conducted sometimes every other year, sometimes every three years; sometimes candidates were selected in response to natural disasters and anomalous phenomena, and sometimes envoys were dispatched on tours to select them. Even at the time, people already regarded the multiplicity of paths as a problem, leaving scholars uncertain where to turn. Our dynasty’s method of selecting men for office alone preserves the intent of the Zhou at its height. Those in the provinces are selected through their respective provinces; those in the two metropolitan regions are selected through those regions. The interval is invariably three years, and selection invariably gives priority to learning in the classics. Other selections, such as those for the worthy, good, upright, and correct, or for those versed in the classics and accomplished in conduct, have been instituted and discontinued irregularly; nor have they been able to surpass the regular examinations. When the method is consistent, scholars have a settled course of study. Those who select them examine them according to that study; those who employ them…

Your servant Renhe has something to say about this: the talents of men throughout the realm have not differed greatly between ancient times and the present. translation_en:
…and unites them into one. If scholars fail to gain selection here, some may reproach themselves and ultimately abandon their prospects. How, then, could we dare to be anything but careful and apprehensive? We would not merely fail the talented men of today; we fear we would also fail to provide men for future appointments. All the responsibilities we, your servants, bear today are indeed matters of serving our ruler by providing him with men.

The candidates have now been selected, and the record has been completed. The Ministry of Rites may examine them, and the emperor, presiding in person, may examine them; those responsible for appointments may then advance them in due order. Thus, today’s written compositions are the basis of tomorrow’s assessments of achievement; today’s names are those that will appear tomorrow with merit titles, ranks, noble titles, and native places. As for those who repeatedly sit the examinations without being selected, reproach themselves, and ultimately abandon their prospects, the state will indeed be unable to employ them. How, then, could we dare to be anything but careful and apprehensive? Now, with this multitude of talented men and numerous [illegible character; ?]…

世之規闢延英之路于茲得
人盖亦盛矣而
南畿視天下尤先焉維是金陵
諸郡渾淪靈淑之氣始祕于
一隅偏安之陋繼熏于百年
羶羶之陀而不得不濬發于
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序

粵自天厭胡元之穢，以天下全畀我聖祖，拓帝王之舊，開太平之原，于茲有國蓋亦遠矣。自我聖祖洪武甲子，參酌成周選舉之意，爰定鄉試之科，詔天下凡三歲一舉行焉，豐茂世之規，闢延英之路，于茲得人蓋亦盛矣。而南畿視天下尤先焉。維是金陵諸郡，渾淪靈淑之氣，始祕于一隅偏安之陋，繼熏于百年腥羶之阨，而不得不濬發于

Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

Ever since Heaven grew disgusted with the defilement of the non-Han Yuan dynasty and bestowed all under Heaven upon our Sagely Founder, he extended the inherited foundations of emperors and kings and opened the source of Great Peace. Our dynasty has now endured for many years. In the jiazi year of the Hongwu reign [1384], our Sagely Founder considered and adapted the principles of selection for office practiced under the Zhou and thereupon established the Provincial Examination, decreeing that it should be held throughout the realm once every three years. He enriched the institutions of a flourishing age [?] and opened a path for inviting men of talent. Since then, the men recruited have indeed been abundant.

Yet the Southern Metropolitan Region stands foremost in the realm. In the prefectures of Jinling, the undivided spiritual and felicitous vital force was first concealed amid the confines of regimes content to hold one corner of the realm, and then tainted by a hundred years of oppression under the rank odor of alien rule. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:

以
獻增

蓋我
祖宗圖治之典莫大于是而臣等
===
所以區區勉圖報稱于萬一
者亦孰有過于此哉錄成臣
廷相當序諸首簡竊嘗究觀篇

translation_en:
…five men, and we have also had the finest of their compositions printed as a record for presentation to the throne, to enhance the court’s glory, make manifest the transforming influence of imperial virtue, circulate these writings throughout the realm, and commend and encourage future students. Among our imperial ancestors’ institutions for securing good government, none is greater than this. And in our humble efforts to repay even one ten-thousandth of the imperial favor, what could surpass this?
When the record was completed, it fell to your servant Tingxiang to write a preface for its opening pages. I have ventured to examine the ancient writings closely. The means by which the worthy predecessors of the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties and earlier transmitted their glory and made their names illustrious in the world are so remote and distant that they can no longer be set out in order. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
始知脩其經術殊師異習各
嶄表見于世而一切縱橫捭
闔刑名之學大氐皆寢而弗
舉抑而靡揚矣然夷考顓門
之學莫盛于漢建元以後蓋
其去古未遠先王遺風餘澤
猶有存者而上之人又規恢
===
而作厲之故在當時疇人子
弟各守一經終身誦習靡不
安焉如魏相以易禮輔孝宣
董仲舒以春秋匡孝武王式
以三百篇箴昌邑夏侯勝以
尚書授東宮口誦心惟率皆
白首故其所成卓然為□□

之學莫盛于漢建元以後盖

===
而作厲之故在當時疇人子
弟各守一經終身誦習靡不
安焉如魏相以易禮轅孝宣
董仲舒以春秋匡孝武王式
以三百篇箴昌邑夏侯勝以
尚書授東宮口誦心惟率皆
足以致其所成卓然為
punctuated: 始知脩其經術，殊師異習，各嶄表見于世，而一切縱橫捭闔、刑名之學，大氐皆寢而弗舉，抑而靡揚矣。然夷考顓門之學，莫盛于漢建元以後。蓋其去古未遠，先王遺風餘澤猶有存者，而上之人又規恢而作厲之，故在當時，疇人子弟各守一經，終身誦習，靡不安焉。如魏相以《易》《禮》輔孝宣，董仲舒以《春秋》匡孝武，王式以三百篇箴昌邑，夏侯勝以《尚書》授東宮，口誦心惟，率皆白首，故其所成卓然為□□
translation_en:
…only then did scholars come to understand the cultivation of classical learning. Following different teachers and pursuing different traditions of study, each distinguished himself in the world, while the various teachings of diplomatic maneuvering and persuasion, and of punishments and administrative accountability, were for the most part laid aside and left unpracticed, suppressed and no longer promoted. Yet, upon careful examination, the learning of specialized scholarly lineages was never more flourishing than in the Han dynasty from the Jianyuan era onward. That age was not yet far removed from antiquity: something of the former kings’ inherited influence and beneficence still remained, and those above further broadened and stimulated this learning. Thus, at that time, the sons and younger members of hereditary scholarly families each adhered to a single classic, reciting and studying it throughout their lives, all content in that pursuit.

For example, Wei Xiang assisted Emperor Xiaoxuan through the Book of Changes and the rites classics; Dong Zhongshu guided Emperor Xiaowu through the Spring and Autumn Annals; Wang Shi admonished the Prince of Changyi through the Three Hundred Odes; and Xiahou Sheng taught the Book of Documents to the crown prince. Reciting with their mouths and pondering in their hearts, almost all continued until their hair turned white. Thus their attainments were outstanding, making them [two illegible characters]…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
焉逮及隋唐始依緣古道設
科取士然亦不能純用經術
詞華是競心耳淺傳六學從
此微矣有宋百有餘年群儒
輩出講明羽翼而後吾先王
所以治天下之大經大法煥
然以明矣顧其時甫好而輒
疎方崇而遽禁君子不無遺
憾焉施我
明興
聖祖
神宗所以尊重經術嘉禮學士大
夫之意又過前代遠甚
今上皇帝篤于繼述尤惓惓焉茲

punctuated: 焉。逮及隋唐，始依緣古道，設科取士，然亦不能純用經術，詞華是競，心耳淺傳，六學從此微矣。有宋百有餘年，群儒輩出，講明羽翼，而後吾先王所以治天下之大經大法煥然以明矣。顧其時甫好而輒疎，方崇而遽禁，君子不無遺憾焉。施我明興，聖祖神宗所以尊重經術、嘉禮學士大夫之意，又過前代遠甚。今上皇帝篤于繼述，尤惓惓焉。茲
translation_en:
… thus. By the Sui and Tang dynasties, men began to follow ancient precedents and establish examination categories for recruiting officials. Yet they could not rely exclusively on learning in the Classics: candidates competed in literary ornament, while transmission through mind and ear remained shallow [?]. The six branches of learning declined from this point onward. After more than a hundred years of the Song dynasty, Confucian scholars emerged in succession, elucidating and supporting this learning. Only then did the great guiding principles and laws by which our former kings governed the realm shine forth clearly. Yet in those times, scarcely had this learning gained favor before it was neglected; just as it was being honored, it was suddenly prohibited. Gentlemen could not but feel regret.

With the rise of our Ming dynasty [?], the commitment of the sage progenitor and divine ancestor to honoring classical learning and treating scholars and scholar-officials with gracious ceremony far surpassed that of previous dynasties. His Majesty the present emperor is deeply committed to carrying forward their work and is especially solicitous in this regard. Now …

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
爾諸士褒然為有司舉首值
文教攸先之所有同升諸公之
期其尚豫思行其所學以荅
我
列聖惓勤期待之厚望也哉是故
治易及禮必如相若京房以
術數取敗戴聖以不法見尤
===
吾無望焉治春秋必如仲舒
若公孫弘之欺世吕步舒之
慘刻吾無望焉治詩必如式
若申公之無益治亂匡衡之
持禄保位吾無望焉治尚書
必如勝若歐陽歙之受賕而
敗李尋之嗜𢦤而流吾無望

爾諸士褎然爲有司舉首値
文教攸先之所有同升諸公之
期其尚豫思行其所學以荅
我
列聖懃勤期待之厚望也哉是故
治易及禮必如相若京房以
術數取敗戴聖以不法見尤

punctuated: 爾諸士褒然為有司舉，首值文教攸先之所，有同升諸公之期，其尚豫思行其所學，以荅我列聖惓勤期待之厚望也哉！是故治易及禮，必如相；若京房以術數取敗，戴聖以不法見尤，吾無望焉。治春秋，必如仲舒；若公孫弘之欺世，吕步舒之慘刻，吾無望焉。治詩，必如式；若申公之無益治亂，匡衡之持禄保位，吾無望焉。治尚書，必如勝；若歐陽歙之受賕而敗，李尋之嗜𢦤而流，吾無望
translation_en:
…you scholars have been honorably selected by the responsible officials. At the outset, you find yourselves in a place where literary education takes precedence, with the prospect of advancing together into public office. Should you not now consider how to put your learning into practice, thereby answering the high hopes that our successive sage emperors have so earnestly placed in you?

Thus, in studying the Book of Changes and the rites, you must emulate Xiang. If, like Jing Fang, you bring ruin upon yourselves through divinatory techniques, or, like Dai Sheng, incur censure through unlawful conduct, I have no hope for you. In studying the Spring and Autumn Annals, you must emulate Zhongshu. If you practice Gongsun Hong’s deception of the world or Lü Bushu’s cruelty, I have no hope for you. In studying the Book of Odes, you must emulate Shi. If, like Master Shen, you contribute nothing to bringing order out of disorder, or, like Kuang Heng, merely cling to your stipend and safeguard your position, I have no hope for you. In studying the Book of Documents, you must emulate Sheng. If, like Ouyang Xi, you accept bribes and come to ruin, or, like Li Xun, indulge a taste for killing [?] and suffer exile, I have no hope…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
焉若然庶不負我
國家開科之意而臣等奉
命求賢之責亦或可以少塞于
他日矣爾諸士其尚勗之哉
或者謂
今治化隆盛遠配唐虞三代而
皇上特輟經帷法從之臣不遠數
===
千里而來者亦惟豫求所謂
唐虞三代之佐焉耳矣是奚
取于炎漢諸臣若彼云云而
已哉噫不然凡臣之所論蓋
就其所業者云耳若繇此而
進之與咎繇稷卨伊傅周召
之儔齊隆等盛固諸士子之

之儔齊隆等盛固諸士子之
punctuated:
焉。若然，庶不負我國家開科之意，而臣等奉命求賢之責，亦或可以少塞于他日矣。爾諸士其尚勗之哉！
或者謂：「今治化隆盛，遠配唐虞三代，而皇上特輟經帷法從之臣，不遠數千里而來者，亦惟豫求所謂唐虞三代之佐焉耳矣。是奚取于炎漢諸臣若彼云云而已哉？」
噫！不然。凡臣之所論，蓋就其所業者云耳。若繇此而進之，與咎繇、稷、卨、伊、傅、周、召之儔齊隆等盛，固諸士子之
translation_en:
… If this is so, we may hope not to fail our dynasty’s purpose in establishing the examinations; and in days to come, we your servants may perhaps have fulfilled, in some small measure, our charge to seek worthy men by imperial command. You scholars, strive to this end!
Some might say: “Today, government and moral transformation flourish, matching the distant ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. His Majesty has specially released ministers serving as Classics lecturers and court attendants from their duties to come here, undeterred by a journey of several thousand li, solely to seek in advance men like the illustrious assistants of those ages. Why, then, merely draw upon those ministers of the Han, the dynasty of Fire, and speak of them at such length?”
Ah, this is not so! All that I, your servant, have discussed concerns only the particular studies in which these men engaged. As for advancing from this foundation to equal the eminence and greatness of such men as Gaoyao, Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, that surely depends upon you scholars’ …

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
趨向若何而非臣等之所敢
知也然自
今日稽古右文而觀之則唐虞
三代之佐臣等詎敢謂必無
其人哉是舉也提調則應天
府尹臣宸府丞臣斌監試則
監察御史臣珮臣崧同考則
===

維新教諭臣夷山臣坤臣鳴鳳臣應禎
臣朝毅其諸執事姓名已具載
錄中故不著
翰林院侍講學士奉訓大夫
李廷相謹序

punctuated:
趨向若何，而非臣等之所敢知也。然自今日稽古右文而觀之，則唐虞三代之佐，臣等詎敢謂必無其人哉？是舉也，提調則應天府尹臣宸、府丞臣斌；監試則監察御史臣珮、臣崧；同考則教授臣昆、學正臣麟、臣惟遠、臣維新、教諭臣夷山、臣坤、臣鳴鳳、臣應禎、臣朝毅。其諸執事姓名已具載錄中，故不著。
翰林院侍講學士奉訓大夫李廷相謹序。
translation_en:
…depends on the direction of the candidates’ aspirations; it is not something that we, your servants, dare presume to know. Yet, considering the present commitment to studying antiquity and honoring letters, how could we dare assert that there are certainly no men comparable to the ministers who assisted the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties?
For this examination, the Proctors were your servants Chen, Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, and Bin, Assistant Prefect. The officials overseeing the examination were your servants Pei and Song, Investigating Censors. 述而不作信而好古竊比於我老彭
故至誠無息不息則久久則徵徵則悠遠
悠遠則博厚博厚則高明

punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

述而不作，信而好古，竊比於我老彭。

故至誠無息。不息則久，久則徵，徵則悠遠，悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。

布帛長短同，則賈相若；麻縷絲絮輕重同，則賈相若；五穀多寡同，則賈相若；屨大小同，則賈相若。曰：「夫物之不齊，物之情也。」

易

顯比之吉，位正中也。

九三，井渫不食，為我心惻；可用汲，王明，並受其福。

易者，象也；象也者，像也。

變動不居，周流六虛，上下无常，剛柔相易。

書

食哉惟時，柔遠能邇，惇德允元，而難任人，蠻夷率服。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“I transmit rather than create; I trust in and cherish antiquity. I venture privately to compare myself to our old Peng.”

Thus perfect sincerity never ceases. Never ceasing, it endures; enduring, it becomes manifest; becoming manifest, it extends far and long; extending far and long, it becomes broad and substantial; becoming broad and substantial, it becomes lofty and luminous.

“If cloth and silk are of equal length, their prices should be similar; if hemp thread and silk floss are of equal weight, their prices should be similar; if the five grains are of equal quantity, their prices should be similar; if shoes are of equal size, their prices should be similar.” He replied: “That things are unequal is inherent in their nature.”

Book of Changes (Yi)

The good fortune of “manifest union” arises because the position is correct and central.

Nine in the third place: The well has been cleared, but no one drinks from it; this makes my heart sorrowful. Its water can be drawn. If the king is enlightened, all will share its blessings.

The Changes consists of images; images are likenesses.

Changing and moving without rest, it circulates through the six empty positions. Its ascent and descent follow no fixed pattern; the firm and yielding exchange places.

Book of Documents (Shu)

As for food, attend to the proper seasons. Be gentle toward those far away and cultivate good relations with those nearby. Honor the virtuous, trust the good, and make it difficult for flatterers to gain office; then the Man and Yi peoples will all submit.

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
惟尹躬暨湯咸有一德克享天心受天明
命以有九有之師
弘于天若德裕乃身不廢在王命
惟敬五刑以成三德一人有慶兆民賴之
其寧惟永
詩
有杕之杜生于道左彼君子兮噬肯適我
中心好之曷飲食之
維南有箕不可以簸揚維北有斗不可以
挹酒漿維南有箕載翕其舌維北有斗
西柄之揭
匪手攜之言示之事匪面命之言提其耳
明明魯侯克明其德既作泮宮淮夷攸服
矯矯虎臣在泮獻馘淑問如臯陶在泮
獻囚濟濟多士克廣德心桓桓于征狄
彼東南烝烝皇皇不吳不揚不告于訩
在泮獻功角弓其觼束矢其搜戎車孔
博徒御無斁既克淮夷孔淑不逆式固

匪手攜之言示之事匪面命之言提其耳
明明魯侯克明其德既作泮宮淮夷攸服
矯矯虎臣在泮獻馘淑問如臯陶在泮
獻囚濟濟多士克廣德心桓桓于征狄
彼東南烝烝皇皇不吳不揚不告于訩
在泮獻功角弓其觩束矢其搜戎車孔
博徒御無斁既克淮夷孔淑不逆式固
punctuated:
惟尹躬暨湯咸有一德，克享天心，受天明命，以有九有之師。
弘于天，若德裕乃身，不廢在王命。
惟敬五刑，以成三德。一人有慶，兆民賴之，其寧惟永。
詩
有杕之杜，生于道左。彼君子兮，噬肯適我？中心好之，曷飲食之？
維南有箕，不可以簸揚；維北有斗，不可以挹酒漿。維南有箕，載翕其舌；維北有斗，西柄之揭。
匪手攜之，言示之事；匪面命之，言提其耳。
明明魯侯，克明其德。既作泮宮，淮夷攸服。矯矯虎臣，在泮獻馘。淑問如臯陶，在泮獻囚。濟濟多士，克廣德心。桓桓于征，狄彼東南。烝烝皇皇，不吳不揚。不告于訩，在泮獻功。角弓其觼，束矢其搜。戎車孔博，徒御無斁。既克淮夷，孔淑不逆。式固
translation_en:
Yin himself and Tang both possessed a single, undivided virtue. They could win Heaven’s heart and receive Heaven’s bright mandate, thereby coming to possess the multitudes of the nine regions.
Enlarge your obedience to Heaven; follow virtue and enrich your own person. Do not neglect the king’s commands.
Reverently administer the five punishments so as to perfect the three virtues. When the One Man enjoys blessings, the myriad people benefit from them, and their peace will endure forever.

Book of Odes
A solitary pear tree grows to the left of the road. That gentleman—would he be willing to visit me? In my heart I cherish him; why should I not give him food and drink?
In the south is the Winnowing Basket, yet it cannot winnow grain; in the north is the Dipper, yet it cannot ladle wine or drink. In the south is the Winnowing Basket, stretching out its tongue; in the north is the Dipper, its handle raised to the west.
Not only did I lead him by the hand; I showed him how things were done. Not only did I instruct him face to face; I took him by the ear.
Illustrious is the lord of Lu, able to make his virtue shine. Having built the Pan Palace, he brought the Huai Yi into submission. His mighty, tiger-like warriors presented severed enemy ears at Pan. Those whose good reputation equalled Gao Yao’s presented prisoners at Pan. The many dignified officers could extend their virtuous purpose. Martial and imposing on campaign, they subdued those in the southeast. Advancing in multitudes, splendid in bearing, they were neither clamorous nor boastful. They did not report their achievements with contentious talk, but presented the fruits of victory at Pan. Their horn bows were fitted with buckles [?], their bundles of arrows gathered together. Their war chariots were very numerous; their foot soldiers and charioteers were tireless. Having overcome the Huai Yi, they treated them with great kindness, without opposition. Thus make firm …

爾猶淮夷卒獲翩彼飛鴞集于泮林食
我桑黮懷我好音憬彼淮夷來獻其琛
元龜象齒大賂南金
春秋
初獻六羽隱公五年春王正月作三軍
襄公十一年
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
幽莊公二十七年冬十有二月公會
齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男邢侯曹
===

曹伯衛人邾人伐齊五月戊寅宋師
及齊師戰于甗齊師敗績俱僖公十八

爾猶，淮夷卒獲。翩彼飛鴞，集于泮林，食我桑黮，懷我好音。憬彼淮夷，來獻其琛：元龜、象齒，大賂南金。

春秋

初獻六羽。隱公五年。春，王正月，作三軍。襄公十一年。

夏，六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯，同盟于幽。莊公二十七年。冬，十有二月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、邢侯、曹伯于淮。僖公十六年。春，王正月，宋公、曹伯、衛人、邾人伐齊。五月，戊寅，宋師及齊師戰于甗，齊師敗績。俱僖公十八年。五月，癸丑，公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子，盟于踐土。冬，公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、陳子、莒子、邾子、秦人于溫。俱僖公二十八年。春，王二月，秦人入滑。夏，四月，辛巳，晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽。俱僖公三十三年。
translation_en:
…your plans; the Huai Yi will finally be subdued. Those owls fly lightly and settle in the woods of Pan. They eat our mulberries and respond to us with pleasing calls. Those distant Huai Yi come to present their treasures: great tortoise shells and elephant tusks, with lavish gifts of gold from the south.

Spring and Autumn Annals

For the first time, six rows of dancers performed the feather dance. Fifth year of Duke Yin.

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, three armies were established. Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.

In summer, in the sixth month, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and they jointly concluded a covenant at You. Twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang.

In winter, in the twelfth month, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Marquis of Xing, and the Earl of Cao at Huai. Sixteenth year of Duke Xi.

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Cao, and men of Wei and Zhu attacked Qi. In the fifth month, on the wuyin day, the army of Song fought the army of Qi at Yan; the army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. Both passages are from the eighteenth year of Duke Xi.

In the fifth month, on the guichou day, the duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and they concluded a covenant at Jiantu. In winter, the duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Chen, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and men of Qin at Wen. Both passages are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.

In spring, in the second month of the royal calendar, men of Qin entered Hua. In summer, in the fourth month, on the xinsi day, men of Jin and the Jiang Rong defeated Qin at Xiao. Both passages are from the thirty-third year of Duke Xi.

text:

吳伐我哀公八年

張而不弛文武弗能也弛而不張文武弗
爲也一張一弛文武之道也
師乎前吾語女乎君子明於禮樂舉而錯

楚子伐鄭，晉郤缺帥師救鄭。宣公九年。
吳伐我。哀公八年。

禮記
是故治世之音安以樂，其政和。
張而不弛，文武弗能也；弛而不張，文武弗爲也。一張一弛，文武之道也。
師乎，前！吾語女乎！君子明於禮樂，舉而錯之而已。
君子隱而顯，不矜而莊，不厲而威，不言而信。

translation_en:
The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. Xi Que of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. Ninth year of Duke Xuan.
Wu attacked our state. Eighth year of Duke Ai.

Book of Rites
Thus, the music of a well-governed age is tranquil and joyful: its government is harmonious.
To keep the bow drawn without relaxing it was beyond even Kings Wen and Wu; to relax it without drawing it was something Kings Wen and Wu would not do. Alternating tension and relaxation was the way of Kings Wen and Wu.
“Shi, come forward! Let me tell you: the gentleman understands rites and music clearly and simply puts them into practice.”
The gentleman, though unobtrusive, is manifest; without self-importance, he is dignified; without severity, he inspires awe; without speaking, he commands trust.

Second Session
Discourse
The sage’s methods for inspiring and stirring the myriad people.

One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose, as if for the Han court, an edict dispatching the Receptionist Chen Nong to seek out surviving books throughout the realm. Second year of the Heping era.
Compose, as if for the Tang court, a proclamation appointing Yao Yuanzhi, Prefect of Tongzhou, as Minister of War and Grand Councilor with the designation “concurrently holding third rank with the Secretariat and Chancellery.” First year of the Kaiyuan era.

擬輔臣謝
賜繩愆糾繆銀圖書表永樂二十二年
判語五條
同寮代判署文案

在官求索借貸人財物
第叁場
===
策五道
問有一代之興必有一代之典以維持人
心昭視久遠如唐虞有典謨夏禹有典
則商有謨訓周有禮制尚矣降及漢唐
宋元亦有三章六典會要經世等作君
子不能無議焉恭惟我
孝宗敬皇帝嘗命儒臣纂輯
累朝典制勒成一書名曰
大明會典

punctuated:
擬輔臣謝賜繩愆糾繆銀圖書表，永樂二十二年。
判語五條：同寮代判署文案；私造斛斗秤尺；收藏禁書及私習天文；宿衞守衞人私自代替；在官求索借貸人財物。
第叁場
策五道
問：有一代之興，必有一代之典，以維持人心，昭視久遠。如唐虞有典謨，夏禹有典則，商有謨訓，周有禮制，尚矣。降及漢唐宋元，亦有三章、六典、會要、經世等作，君子不能無議焉。恭惟我孝宗敬皇帝嘗命儒臣纂輯累朝典制，勒成一書，名曰《大明會典》。
translation_en:
Draft a memorial in the voice of a senior minister expressing thanks for the bestowal of a silver seal inscribed “Correct faults and rectify errors,” dated to the twenty-second year of Yongle (1424).
Five legal judgments: a colleague adjudicating and signing case documents on another’s behalf; privately manufacturing grain measures, scales, and measuring rules; possessing prohibited books and privately studying astronomy; personnel on palace or other guard duty privately arranging substitutes; officials soliciting or borrowing other people’s money or property while in office.
Third Session
Five policy questions
Question: Whenever a dynasty arises, it must have its own institutions and statutes to sustain the allegiance of the people and provide clear guidance for ages to come. Thus, Tang and Yu had their canons and counsels; Yu of Xia had his statutes and rules; Shang had its counsels and instructions; and Zhou had its ritual institutions. These go back to high antiquity. Later, under the Han, Tang, Song, and Yuan, there were also such works as the Three Articles, the Six Statutes, the Collected Essentials, and the Compendium for Governing the World. Yet gentlemen have not been without reservations about them. We reverently recall that our Emperor Xiaozong Jing once commanded Confucian court scholars to compile the institutions and regulations of successive reigns into a single book, entitled the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian)…

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
今上皇帝又命儒臣重加是正刋示中外甚盛
典也不知與典謨典則諸書同歟異歟
抑是書大氐準諸司職掌而作而
御製諸書附焉中間損益因革之大亦有可
得而言者歟夫職掌一書乃我
太祖高皇帝斟酌周禮而作者規模宏遠品式
精詳治天下之大經大法盖靡不具焉
而又奚待于會典之作歟說者謂事更
數聖世更
===

先朝亦嘗有志纂述而事弗克竟意者
天將有待於
二聖人歟夫莫為于前雖美弗彰莫為于後雖
盛弗傳我

神孫先後一心創守一道皆於是乎見焉爾諸
士子其鋪張揚厲之以見我

punctuated: 今上皇帝又命儒臣重加是正，刋示中外，甚盛典也。不知與典謨、典則諸書同歟異歟？抑是書大氐準諸司職掌而作，而御製諸書附焉，中間損益因革之大，亦有可得而言者歟？夫職掌一書，乃我太祖高皇帝斟酌周禮而作者，規模宏遠，品式精詳，治天下之大經大法，盖靡不具焉，而又奚待于會典之作歟？說者謂事更數聖，世更數代，會典一書有不容不作者，其果然歟否歟？先朝亦嘗有志纂述，而事弗克竟，意者天將有待於二聖人歟？夫莫為于前，雖美弗彰；莫為于後，雖盛弗傳。我聖祖神孫，先後一心，創守一道，皆於是乎見焉。爾諸士子，其鋪張揚厲之，以見我
translation_en:
The present Emperor has further commanded Confucian officials to revise and correct it anew, and to print and promulgate it throughout the capital and the provinces—a most magnificent undertaking indeed. We wonder: is it similar to, or different from, such writings as the Canons and Counsels and the Canons and Rules? Moreover, this book was largely compiled on the basis of the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang), with imperially authored works appended. Can the major additions and omissions, continuities and changes within it also be identified and discussed? The Duties of the Various Offices was composed by our Emperor Taizu Gao after careful consideration of the Rites of Zhou. Vast and far-reaching in conception, precise and detailed in its categories and prescriptions, it contains virtually all the fundamental principles and great laws for governing the realm. Why, then, was the compilation of the Collected Statutes still necessary? Some say that affairs have passed through the hands of several sage rulers and time has passed through several reigns, making the compilation of the Collected Statutes indispensable. Is this truly so or not?

A previous reign also saw an intention to compile this work, but the undertaking could not be completed. Might Heaven have been waiting for the two sages? If no one undertakes the work beforehand, its excellence, however great, cannot be made manifest; if no one undertakes the work afterward, its grandeur, however great, cannot be transmitted. Our sage ancestor and his divine descendants, sharing one purpose across successive reigns and following one Way in founding and preserving the dynasty, are all revealed here. title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
明之治之所以盛
問官多則民擾省則賦輕其理有不可易
者唐虞稽古建官惟百夏商官倍亦克
用乂不可尚矣說者謂成周官制最爲
詳備今周禮一書其跡固在攷其六官
之屬每事必設畿甸之內眾至五萬餘

問：官多則民擾，省則賦輕，其理有不可易者。唐虞稽古，建官惟百；夏商官倍，亦克用乂，不可尚矣。說者謂成周官制最爲詳備。今《周禮》一書，其跡固在。攷其六官之屬，每事必設，畿甸之內，眾至五萬餘人。不知當時官何以給，民何以堪歟？兵多則財耗，少則勢分，其勢有必至者。咎繇佐舜，五服攸明；公旦輔周，六軍是作，不可復矣。說者謂西漢兵灋最爲近古。今班固一書，其制固存。攷其征伐之將，因事而置；京師之兵，纔盈萬人。不知當時國胡以強，民胡以安歟？夫周之制善矣，而未免有民擾之慮；漢之灋良矣，而未免有兵弱之虞。諒茲俊髦，必有讜論。

問：君子論天下之事與天下之人，蓋亦難矣。然亦顧其時勢與其所自處何如爾。姑以史冊所疑數事，與爾諸士子商之。
translation_en:
…why the governance of our Ming is so flourishing.

Question: When officials are numerous, the people are harassed; when their number is reduced, taxation is light. There is an immutable principle here. The rulers of Tang and Yu examined antiquity and established only a hundred offices; Xia and Shang doubled that number, yet likewise achieved good order. These achievements cannot be surpassed. Commentators say that the official system of Zhou was the most detailed and complete. Its traces certainly remain in the surviving book, the Rites of Zhou. Examining the personnel attached to its six ministries, we find that officials were established for every undertaking, their numbers within the royal domain reaching more than fifty thousand. How, then, were these officials supported, and how could the people bear the burden?

When troops are numerous, resources are depleted; when they are few, strength is dispersed. These are inevitable consequences of the circumstances. Gao Yao assisted Shun, and the five zones of service were clearly defined; Duke Dan assisted Zhou, and the six armies were established. Such achievements could not be repeated. Commentators say that the military system of the Western Han came closest to that of antiquity. Its institutions certainly survive in Ban Gu’s book, the History of the Han. Examining its arrangements, we find that generals for military campaigns were appointed as occasions arose, while troops in the capital barely numbered ten thousand. How, then, was the state made strong and the people kept secure? Zhou’s institutions were sound, yet concerns about harassment of the people remained unavoidable; Han’s methods were good, yet fears of military weakness remained unavoidable. Surely you outstanding talents will have forthright arguments to offer.

Question: For a gentleman to judge the affairs of the world and its people is indeed difficult. Yet this depends upon the circumstances of their times and how they situated themselves within them. Let us take several doubtful matters in the historical records and discuss them with you candidates.

title: 正德十一年應天府鄉試錄
text:
夫匈奴未滅何以家爲是也而或乃多
請田宅何歟入府端坐召斬弄臣是也
而或乃望塵下拜何歟詩書禮樂足以
彊晉矣而作文賦者何以有河橋之敗
禮義廉耻足以霸齊矣而作四維論者
何以有伾文之附蕭曹舊隙胡何卒而
參相張陳舊德胡耳王而餘戮記書三
篋與藏書萬卷者其事君孰優教子以
襴與遺子以經者其傳家孰善或以布
===
被而取譏或以布被而見美孰得乎或
用鉤距而得事情或用鉤距而固君寵
孰賢乎或勸舉進士而不應與勸無舉
進士而不從者其故何歟或勸見宰相
而不肯與上書宰相而不嫌者其故何
歟從帝至咸陽而獨收圖籍與從主征
伐而獨收人物者其見孰高大將軍尊
重而獨長揖與相王尊重而輒下拜者
其爲孰是不從三國之言而竟達漢天
